     2	# WP-005: GUI "Text Only" tab in dialogue modal
     3	
     4	## Plan Context
     5	
     6	This plan delivers a CLI extraction script and a GUI "Text Only" tab that make LangGraph agent dialogue readable without parsing raw JSONL, sharing a common `.md` output format.
     7	
     8	## Description
     9	
    10	Add the frontend "Text Only" tab to the chunk dialogue modal — including the API client method, tab bar UI with lazy-loading logic, CSS styling, and version query string bumps. When viewing a chunk dialogue, users see a two-tab layout (Detailed / Text Only) with the existing structured view as the default and lazily-loaded prose on the Text Only tab.
    11	
    12	## Scope
    13	
    14	- `mcp-server/gui/public/api-client.js` — new `getChunkText()` method
    15	- `mcp-server/gui/public/views/project-detail-dialogues.js` — tab bar injection and tab-switch logic in `_openDialogueModal()`
    16	- `mcp-server/gui/public/styles.css` — `.dialogue-modal-tabs` and `.dialogue-tab` CSS rules
    17	- `mcp-server/gui/public/index.html` — version query string bumps on changed script tags
    18	
    19	## Deliverables
    20	
    21	- `API.getChunkText(repo, slug, filename)` method in `api-client.js` that calls `GET /projects/:repo/:slug/chunks/:filename/text` and returns `data.content`
    22	- Tab bar HTML (`.dialogue-modal-tabs` div with two `<button class="dialogue-tab">` elements) injected between the modal header and body when `useChunks === true`
    23	- Tab-switch click handler (delegated on tab container) that:
    24	  - Shows/hides the Detailed content panel and the Text Only content panel
    25	  - On first "Text Only" click: shows a loading indicator, calls `API.getChunkText()`, renders the result via `marked.parse(text)` in a `div.dialogue-markdown` wrapper, and caches the rendered HTML in a JS variable
    26	  - On subsequent "Text Only" clicks: displays the cached content without re-fetching
    27	- Legacy path (`useChunks === false`) remains unchanged — no tab bar rendered
    28	- CSS rules for `.dialogue-modal-tabs`, `.dialogue-tab`, `.dialogue-tab.active`, and `.dialogue-tab:hover:not(.active)` using existing CSS custom property tokens (no dark-mode overrides needed)
    29	- Version query string bumps (`?v=N` incremented) on `api-client.js` and `project-detail-dialogues.js` script tags in `index.html`
    30	
    31	## Dependencies
    32	
    33	- WP-004
    34	
    35	## Acceptance Criteria
    36	
    37	1. When useChunks === true, the dialogue modal displays a two-tab bar with "Detailed" (default active) and "Text Only" buttons between the header and body
    38	2. Clicking the "Text Only" tab fetches extracted prose via API.getChunkText() and renders it as HTML via marked.parse() in a .dialogue-markdown wrapper
    39	3. The "Text Only" tab content is cached in a JS variable — subsequent tab switches within the same modal session do not re-fetch from the API
    40	4. When useChunks === false (legacy Markdown dialogues), no tab bar is rendered and behaviour is unchanged
    41	5. All user-derived strings in the tab UI are escaped via escapeHtml() and all JS follows ES5 conventions (var, function, .then() — no arrow functions, const/let, or template literals)
    42	6. CSS tab styles use existing CSS custom property tokens (--color-border, --color-text-muted, --color-text, --color-link) that auto-adapt to dark mode
    43	7. Version query strings on api-client.js and project-detail-dialogues.js script tags in index.html are incremented
    44	
    45	## Active Pipeline Stages
    46	
    47	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    48	
    49	## Estimated Complexity
    50	
    51	Medium
    52	
    53	## Rationale
    54	
    55	Adding a second tab to the existing modal is the least disruptive UI change — the Detailed view is completely unchanged. Lazy-loading the text tab avoids a wasted network request for users who only need the Detailed view (the common case). The tab bar sits between header and body as its own layout row, keeping the header clean (title + close always visible) and following standard tab UI patterns.
    56	
    57	## Rejected Approaches
    58	
    59	- *Eager loading (fetch both tabs on modal open)* — rejected because it wastes a network request when the user only needs the Detailed view, which is the common case.
    60	- *Tabs inside header or content-toggle buttons* — rejected because placing the tab bar in the header would crowd the title/close area, and toggle buttons are less discoverable than a standard tab pattern.
    61	- *Stdout output instead of file caching* — rejected because the endpoint needs to return structured JSON, and stdout doesn't save files as required.
